title: Crossbreeding
text: “Buu, buu.”
Lazy Pig was making some kind of noise.
“So the plan is to throw in some pity-appeal poses too, just to satisfy that crowd a bit?”
“If it’s an order, I’ll do it, but…”
“Ugh, no way. Sniffing super spicy stuff or rotten smells, no thanks.”
“We’re not doing that!”

Apparently, on Lazy Pig’s suggestion, they were going to have someone sniff something pungent and make a show of disgust, just enough to satisfy the customers who came for that sort of abuse-flavored entertainment. Aside from that bit, the rest could apparently be a perfectly normal act.
“Then how about I let you sniff some stinky socks, Naofumi? You’d probably just stand there with your mouth hanging open.”
Ren shot back sarcastically. Honestly, I couldn’t help but think that sort of thing would suit Father strangely well.
“What if I did the Flehmen response? Who exactly is asking for that? Where’s the demand coming from?”
For a moment I wondered if Ark might do it for me, but… he probably wouldn’t. Even if I waved a cat toy in front of him, he’d just smile pleasantly. Father seemed far more likely to indulge me there.
“Anyway, I made food for everyone, so eat up already. Today it’s stew—heard Ren likes it.”
“I can already tell from the smell that I hate it. And don’t think you can win me over with food!”
Even as he said that, Ren’s tail was wagging happily.
“The delicious food big brothers made!”
“Wooof!”

Keel and Wolf were the same. Watching this, even the onlookers—Éclair included—seemed to unanimously agree that anyone would assume these three were one and the same group. Anyway, Ren really was settling into circus life quite nicely these days.
And so, as night deepened… morning came.
“Waaaaaaah!”
Ren’s scream, as had become routine every morning.
“Hey, Motoyasu! Do something about training Luna already! She had me sleeping next to Keel again!”
Ren came storming in to complain, still a bit out of breath. Keel, freshly woken, shuffled along behind him. And pretending not to hear any of this exchange, Luna-chan trailed along too.
“Ufufu… so cute when she’s all puffed up and angry.”
She looked utterly enraptured. This was Luna-chan’s moment of bliss.
“What seems to be the matter, I say? What complaint could you possibly have about Luna-chan?”
“Of course I have a complaint! Every single day, I wake up and there’s Keel’s sleeping face right in front of me! Do you have any idea how bad it gets when she ends up on top of me!”

I honestly had no idea. Was it something like waking up next to a pig? I’d experienced that myself, once upon a time. Father, too, had struggled with Tiger Girl sneaking into his bed. So what exactly was the problem with Ren and Keel having similar surprises?
“Luna-chan is merely playing matchmaker between you and Keel. Perhaps ask Elephant, or consult with Rafumi.”

To begin with, Luna-chan clearly wished for Ren and Keel’s numbers to increase. Wasn’t that fine, though? Not really my department. Elephant might take Filolial-sama’s delicate concerns to heart and come up with a solution. Or perhaps Rafumi, eager to keep Ren from ending up alone, would be the one to deal with it.
“I’m complaining to you precisely because you’re useless! Do you understand what it feels like, being forced together against your will!”
“I myself was once engaged to a pig, much to my displeasure—so what of it, I say?”

Just thinking about it made me want to retch. Such memories did exist. Incidentally, when I moved, not a single one of them followed. “We’ll wait for you forever!” they’d said, waving me off—every last pig of them. Selfish creatures, the lot of them—quick to sulk and retaliate if displeased, yet lacking the spine to follow when I relocated, while demanding change only from me.
“You heard all that and you’re still just brushing it off!”
“I am simply supporting Luna-chan’s ambitions, I say.”

If Keel and Ren getting together made Luna-chan happy, that seemed fine to me. At least this way, a second Rafumi wouldn’t show up—cause for celebration all around. Hm? Somewhere in my mind, I felt like the previous Father was suggesting that another Rafumi might be sent as an assassin against Luna-chan in order to alter the past, but HAHA, surely I was overthinking things. If we avoided that pitiful Christmas, Ren wouldn’t do such a thing. Now, if it were something like traveling back in time to change a future where some experiment turned him into a pig, that might be plausible. But looking at Ren’s not-entirely-displeased face whenever Keel clung to him, no such thing seemed likely.
“Anyway, if someone moved you while you were sleeping, wouldn’t you normally wake up? Aren’t you just sleeping too deeply?”
“Luna can make sleep go deeper with dark magic~”

Ah, I see. So there was dark magic that made it hard to wake once you’d fallen asleep. This was exactly the sort of thing Kuro-chan wished dark magic could do. …Could it perhaps be used to help Ark fall asleep? Probably not. Would peaceful slumber ever come for that man?
“Whew… hey, sword bro. Aren’t we past the point of resisting? Fighting it is more tiring than just going along with it.”
Keel, still half-asleep, spoke to Ren in a tone of resignation.
“What are you talking about? If we give up now, they’ll seriously force us to… crossbreed!”
He chose his words carefully there.

“That’s not it. I just think if we keep resisting this hard, it’s gonna get more extreme. So it’s better to just act like we’re close and not actually do anything… you gotta think that way or you’ll never get out of it.”
Keel said this with a deep sigh, resting a hand on Ren’s shoulder. Was it just me, or did that sound less like resignation and more like a proposal for conspiracy?
“I think of myself as a guy, and you too, sword bro. Let’s just be friends.”
“O-oh… yeah…”
“Buu… but Keel-kun’s a girl. It’s a perfect match.”

Luna-chan watched this newfound alliance with obvious displeasure. Would it work out? As for me, personally, Keel and Ren getting together didn’t matter to me one way or another, except that it would make Luna-chan happy.
“Anyway, let’s go find Wolf bro! Today we’re gonna go looking for cool stuff with Wolf bro again!”
“No way! If I hang out with him, Naofumi’s gonna start treating us like dogs! You want to get brushed again?”
“Huh? That felt amazing though. You don’t like it, sword bro? Wolf bro practically begs for it. He was even showing his belly to get it done.”
“The thought of a grown man doing that is disgusting! I don’t want to end up like that eventually! I need to get back to being human, fast!”
Ren clutched his head and bolted off in refusal. Naturally, Luna-chan watched the whole scene with a warm, contented smile. She looked utterly happy.
“Sword bro’s got it rough, huh…”
Keel muttered, watching Ren dash off, before heading out for his morning walk. Rabbit Guy, who had been reading a book, seemed to be watching this scene with particular interest.
“Getting brushed by Iwatani-sama… huh.”

Rabbit Guy stared intently at his own arm. Lately, Rabbit Guy had taken to watching Crocodile Guy and Wolf whenever they transformed into their beastman forms. This… it looked very much like Rabbit Guy wanted Father to brush him too. Not that I could talk—I’d had it done before myself. When I asked, in my usaunny form, for Father to pet me, he obliged. Fufun, Father’s brushing was truly excellent, I say. It left one’s coat gleaming and silky. It was also a reward given in turn to the Filolial-sama who participated in the circus. Wolf, in particular, often got brushed and had his coat groomed. And apparently, more recently, Crocodile Guy had started getting his scales cleaned—securing oil and polish and having them carefully buffed, or so I heard.
